sources.title: International Chamber of Commerce
sources.facts_supported: Incoterms(r) 2020 Checklist: FAS/FOB maritime/inland-waterway only; FCA for any mode incl multimodal and terminal delivery; C-group (CFR/CIF/CPT/CIP) are shipment contracts - risk passes on delivery (on board) in seller's country while seller pays main carriage; under CIF seller must arrange minimum-cover cargo insurance (LMA/IUA Clauses C or similar), CIP requires all-risk cover (Clauses A).

sources.title: Singapore Customs
sources.facts_supported: Page updated 26 Feb 2026: new-vehicle customs value starts from CIF/transaction value and adds selling commissions, assists, packing, royalties, freight, insurance; worked FOB->CIF example adds inland transport, handling, overseas freight and insurance; used-vehicle Scenario A adds depreciation + freight + insurance + incidentals, Scenario B valued like new; alternative identical/similar/deductive/computed/residual methods; MAS weekly average FX.

sources.title: Singapore Customs
sources.facts_supported: Updated 26 Feb 2026: 4-step process - customs value assessment, approval letter (unit price/Incoterm), In-Payment (Duty & GST) permit via TradeNet within 3 months declaring N/U/T new/used/taxi and engine/chassis codes, then clear vehicle; road registration handled separately by LTA.

sources.title: Singapore Land Transport Authority
sources.facts_supported: Procedures on Importation & Registration of a Car: from 1 Jan 2025 no new registration of diesel/diesel-NG cars (incl imported used); brand-new vs used classification rules; imported used car must be <=3 years old at registration and pays S$10,000 surcharge; must meet prevailing exhaust/noise standards and pass VETL emission test; documents incl manufacturer invoice, Bill of Lading, Inward Cargo Clearance Permit; VAC issued after inspection before registration.

sources.title: Malaysia Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry
sources.organization: Malaysia Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry
sources.facts_supported: Effective 1 Aug 2019 personal-vehicle Approved Permit (AP) applications via ePermit (Dagang Net); listed fees; classic/vintage need prior written MITI approval. Confirms AP is a national import-licence stage independent of shipping term.

sources.title: ASEAN Secretariat
sources.facts_supported: ASEAN Guidelines on Light Electric Vehicles; baseline probe returned 403 (Sucuri). Not dead, but not readable this session.

claim_source_matrix.CLAIM: FOB risk transfers on board; CIF seller pays main sea carriage and arranges insurance but risk transfers on board in China.
FCA fits pre-loading terminal delivery; CIP fits insured multimodal incl feeder/inland.
Singapore customs value starts from CIF/transaction value and adds freight, insurance, handling and other deliver-to-SG charges; a bare FOB vehicle price is not by itself the taxable customs value.
claim_source_matrix.EXACT_SUPPORT: SG Customs valuation page 26/02/2026 with worked example.

claim_source_matrix.CLAIM: Singapore follows a 4-step import process (value assessment, approval, In-Payment Duty+GST permit via TradeNet declaring N/U/T, clearance) and road registration is then handled separately by LTA.

Singapore: imported used cars must be <=3 years old at registration, pay S$10,000 per-car surcharge, meet emission/noise standards (VETL test), and need B/L + Inward Cargo Clearance Permit; from 1 Jan 2025 new diesel/diesel-NG car registration is not permitted.
Malaysia requires a personal-vehicle Approved Permit via ePermit (effective 1 Aug 2019) - a national import-licence stage independent of Incoterm; a Malaysian AP does not work elsewhere in ASEAN.
